high.title: USD and Oil Price Surge Due to Middle East Conflict: How Will Exchange Rate and Inflation in Vietnam Be Affected?
high.summary: Early morning February 28, 2026, the US coordinated with Israel to conduct airstrikes on Iran. Iran immediately retaliated against US and Israeli-related locations. This escalated Middle East tensions rapidly, increasing global geopolitical risks. Developments immediately impacted commodity markets, with oil prices surging on supply disruption fears. Cross-continental logistics supply chains may also be disrupted due to soaring insurance and shipping costs, causing localized goods shortages. After conflict news broke, the USD Index (DXY) rose 0.8% to 98.42 points, while global gold prices also trended upward, reflecting clear "risk-off" sentiment in global financial markets. According to VCBS analysis, in an environment of increased geopolitical uncertainty, global capital flows tend to reallocate toward holding safe-haven assets like USD and gold.

high.title: Middle East Tensions Impact USD Price: What Effects?
high.summary: USD appreciation pressure from Middle East conflict. In Vietnam, the USD exchange rate has recently shown signs of increase. The State Bank currently announces a central rate of 25,057 dong/USD, up 13 dong consecutively over the past week. At commercial banks, USD is commonly quoted around 26,029-26,309 dong/USD (buy-sell). In the free market, USD trades at higher levels around 26,850-26,880 dong/USD. This development reflects the USD's strengthening trend internationally amid rising geopolitical risks. At a recent government press conference, SBV Deputy Governor Pham Thanh Ha said escalating Middle East tensions have caused global oil prices to surge 8-13% in just a few days, creating additional inflationary pressure globally. According to Ha, in this context, many major central banks are being more cautious about interest rate cuts, with some even signaling potential rate increases to control inflation.

high.title: Government Bond Yields: Safe Haven Channel for Capital Flows Amid Market Turbulence
high.summary: February 2026 recorded remarkable breakthrough in public debt issuance activity. According to HNX data, the State Treasury organized 12 auction sessions, successfully raising 34,495 billion dong, recording strong 32.44% growth compared to early year. Cumulative two-month mobilization reached 60,541 billion dong - completing 55% of Q1 plan and about 12% of full-year 2026 target. Despite increased total mobilization, actual auction developments revealed risk appetite differentiation. In February, though the Treasury offered diverse tenures from 5-30 years, the 10-year segment became the new "king" with mobilization success rate consistently above 98%. This reflects investors' preference for the "sweet spot" balancing yield attractiveness with manageable duration risk. The shift toward 10-year bonds as the market favorite demonstrates institutional investors prioritizing the optimal risk-return profile in an environment of heightened uncertainty.

medium.title: VN-Index Loses Over 113 Points in 1 Week, Experts Identify "Oversold" Stock Groups
medium.summary: Vietnam's stock market closed the first trading week of March with poor performance as VN-Index dropped sharply to lowest levels in about three weeks. The index closed March 6 at 1,767 points, losing over 40 points from the previous session and over 113 points from the prior week - similar to the "tariff shock" in April 2025. Selling pressure increased amid escalating Middle East geopolitical tensions, causing extreme investor anxiety.

medium.title: BIDV Interest Rates March 2025: Which Term Has Highest Rates?
medium.summary: For counter deposits, BIDV currently applies 0.1%/year for non-term deposits. For short 1-2 month terms, counter deposit rates are 2.1%/year. 3 and 5-month terms are listed at 2.4%/year. For 6-9 month terms, counter deposit rates increase to 3.5%/year. For 12-month term, BIDV applies 5.2%/year rate. The highest rates of 5.3%/year apply to long-term deposits of 24-36 months.

medium.title: Military Bank Just Raised Savings Interest Rates Significantly
medium.summary: According to the latest deposit rate schedule for individual customers depositing at counters, MB kept rates unchanged for short terms under 12 months but increased rates significantly for terms from 12 months and above. For deposits under 1 billion dong, 12-18 month rates increased from 5.5%/year to 6.1%/year (+0.6pp). For long terms 24-60 months, rates were raised from 6.3%/year to 6.6%/year (+0.3pp).

medium.title: Banks Mobilize Capital
medium.summary: Since early March 2026, numerous commercial banks have adjusted deposit rates higher across multiple terms. VPBank increased savings deposit rates 0.2-0.5 percentage points for terms 6+ months starting March 10. LPBank also adjusted rates up 0.2-0.8 percentage points across all terms from March 3. Sacombank had stronger adjustments, increasing 0.6-1.3 percentage points compared to before.
